items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: and I told Big John I was going to write a tune and name it after him

ctx.x: Well, I think a lot of people that said that -- Fletcher was so prominent during that time, as an arranger, until they just figured that -- (inaudible) well, when you played this tune, Fletcher arranged that, one of those things, until they found out later that that were learning to arrange and were making little things there were other guys in the band (unintelligible) and so

they began to give us credit for it. One of my biggest thrills was a tune that I wrote and we recorded it called "Big John Special," and how it came about -- I got the name from -- there was a guy in New York City that owned a tavern where most musicians and professionals hung out up in Harlem on a 141st and Seventh Avenue. Anybody that was somebody always hung out in Big John's. Musicians didn't play. He just had good food there and beer and all that stuff, and so anybody they wanted to find they'd go find at…

because you had to pay by the mile and it wasn't like the Greyhound -- expensive like that -- so they gave 'em rates, and this particular bus broke down one time, and we had to take a plane to the next job, and while I was up in the air, I was scared anyway, so I took my little stuff out and started writing this particular tune. I hadn't named it Big John then, but this is how it turned out.
